description:
10 ms chunk / 1 s, N streams. membrane_audio_mix_plugin 0.16.5: baseline ClipPreventingAdder, NIF column NativeAdder (C, built locally by bundlex/unifex; unifex resource state). Reproduce ClipPreventingAdder's job (scale down on overflow, hold samples to the next zero crossing), not hard clipping; the hard-clip Adder has no native twin and is a header mention only. Kernel does the inner sum/scale loop; the held-back queue and scale state stay in Elixir (defk-dtw.9). Call init/mix/flush directly (RawAudio via struct!/2 after Mix.install). Agreement: concatenated mix+flush output byte-identical.

Evidence bar (from defk-dtw.4/defk-dtw.15): script examples/<name>.exs with Mix.install of the pinned anchor package; the anchor's Elixir version is the first baseline and must be optimised further in Elixir before the verdict counts (what was tried listed in the header; baseline: :optimized); realistic size declared in the header before any numbers; workload verdict at the realistic size, other size beside; ~6-point geometric sweep with crossover (smallest size where defk >= 2x, or none), skipped if a large run exceeds ~1 min; NIF timing and responsiveness (max and p99 1 ms tick gap, one scheduler, large size, for Elixir/defk/NIF) via Defk.Bench.report/1; Elixir, defk and NIF outputs must agree (failure fails the script); quiet-machine run_all.exs; row added to examples/README.md.

comments.text: Note from 'Which convenience constructs do the six target workloads need?' (defk-dtw.18): the PCM sketch passed the held-back wave into the kernel only for illustration. This ticket's split stands (queue and scale state in Elixir, per defk-dtw.9); the decision that matters is that a data-dependent output length needs no construct (array + count, binary_part in Elixir).

examples/pcm_mix.exs on branch defk-9p6.14/pcm-mixing (96d3866, merged with main in b66ee00; mix ci green). PROVISIONAL numbers, taken while two other benchmark agents loaded the machine (quiet run: defk-sgw.4). M-series, OTP 29, Elixir 1.20.

Realistic size (declared in the header): N = 4 streams, 48 kHz stereo s16le, 10 ms chunks; timed job 1 s of audio = 100 mix calls + flush. Other size: 1 s chunks.
- Verdict (10 ms): optimised Elixir 2.6-2.7 ms, defk 0.41-0.49 ms: 5.4-6.6x, good. NativeAdder (membrane_audio_mix_plugin 0.16.5, C via bundlex/unifex) 0.72-0.75 ms: defk 1.5-1.8x faster.
- 1 s chunks: Elixir 2.4-2.6, defk 0.31-0.37: 6.6-8.5x; NativeAdder 0.68-0.75: defk 1.9-2.5x faster.
- Sweep 1/4/16/64/250/1000 ms chunks: 2.8-3.0x at 1 ms, 5.4-5.6x at 4 ms, 6-8x from 16 ms; crossover 1 ms (smallest size). N = 2/4/8/16: 5.2-5.6x / 6.8-7.4x / 9.3-9.5x / 7.8-10.4x, defk 1.5-2.1x faster than NativeAdder throughout. s32le similar.
- Responsiveness (1 ms ticker, one scheduler, 60 s of audio in 1 s chunks; ticker floor ~2 ms under load): Elixir max 3.2-5.6 ms (p99 3.2-3.4), defk 2.2-2.3 ms, NativeAdder 41-43 ms: each call blocks ~0.7 ms and the 60 back-to-back calls are never preempted (no enif_consume_timeslice).
- Agreement: concatenated mix+flush output byte-identical across ClipPreventingAdder, all Elixir variants, defk and NativeAdder on 144 cases (s16le+s32le, N 1/2/4/8, 1/10/250 ms chunks, 6 signals incl. loud, DC offset, silence, full-scale noise); kernels = Elixir mode on 80 cases. Mismatch raises.

Elixir baseline (optimized), per 1 s audio, 10 ms / 1 s chunks: ClipPreventingAdder 19-20 / 29-30 ms; list-based scan with sums by recursion 6.0, :lists.zipwith 6.3-6.6, Enum.zip_with+Enum.sum 7.0/13-14.5, add from binaries 4.6/4.4; final PCM.Elixir (first two streams summed from binaries, last added inside the scan, output appended per sample, overflowing half-wave cut off and rewritten) 2.6-2.7/2.5; lazy half-wave list 3.2/5.8-15 (rejected). Plus min_heap_size 32 MB for the process (applies to all sides; without it Elixir varies 4-10 ms at 1 s chunks and the plugin 40-70 ms).

Decisions: kernel does sum + clamp (check-free, vectorised) + sign scan with rescale; held-back i64 sums and sign stay in Elixir (defk-dtw.9), kernel returns full arrays + count, Elixir binary_parts. Formats s16le and s32le (f32le: NativeAdder reads f32 bits as ints, no native twin; s24le needs an element type defk lacks). Equal-length buffers only (the two plugin implementations disagree otherwise). The s16/s32 kernels come from one macro. NativeAdder built without problems.

Tickets filed (needs-triage): defk-siy (b[base + i] with a variable block offset keeps its bounds check: the sum loop runs scalar, ~70% of the kernel), defk-xyz (Defk.Report puts every note of a macro-generated kernel on the call line).

title: Target workload: PCM mixing with clip prevention vs Membrane NativeAdder
